Class CommandGenerateCrafting.CraftingGenerationHelper

java.lang.Object
org.cyclops.integratedcrafting.command.CommandGenerateCrafting.CraftingGenerationHelper
Enclosing class:
CommandGenerateCrafting
public static class CommandGenerateCrafting.CraftingGenerationHelper extends Object
Helper class for crafting network generation logic, shared between command and game tests. All presets are built on top of the same grid layout: cable planes at even Y levels, and a checkerboard of cables and free "cells" at odd Y levels. Every cell is a free position that is surrounded by cables of a single network, so it can hold a container or a crafter that is observed or targeted by parts on the surrounding cables. Every cell can carry up to two parts: one on the cable below it (pointing up), and one on a horizontally neighbouring cable (pointing sideways).

  • Field Details

    • RECIPES_PER_INTERFACE

      public static final int RECIPES_PER_INTERFACE
      The number of distinct recipes that fit in a single crafting interface.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • STORAGE_STACKS

      public static final int STORAGE_STACKS
      The number of full stacks of crafting inputs that is placed in every storage chest. This deliberately leaves slots free in every chest. A crafting interface buffers its results until it can push them into network storage, and it stops ticking its jobs entirely while that buffer is non-empty. Completely filled chests would therefore jam every crafting interface after a single craft.
      See Also:
      • Constant Field Values

    • CHAINS

      public static final List<CommandGenerateCrafting.CraftingGenerationHelper.CraftingChain> CHAINS
      All crafting chains that the presets can request. Every chain is a wooden item that is crafted purely out of planks of a single wood species, where those planks are in turn crafted out of a single log of that species. This gives us a large pool of independent chains: the crafting writer aspect refuses to schedule a job for an item that is already being crafted, so every writer in a preset needs its own distinct output item to actually cause load. Only recipes that are shapeless, at most 2x2, or exactly 3 wide are usable here: CraftingGrid fills a 3x3 grid row by row, so a recipe that is 2 wide and 3 tall (such as doors) would end up misaligned.

    • FILLER_RECIPES

      public static final List<net.minecraft.resources.Identifier> FILLER_RECIPES
      Extra recipes that are only used to fill up the recipe slots of crafting interfaces. These are never requested by a crafting writer: their only purpose is to grow the number of recipes that the network's recipe index holds, and that every crafting interface has to evaluate and validate.

    • ALL_RECIPES

      public static final List<net.minecraft.resources.Identifier> ALL_RECIPES
      All recipes that a crafting interface can be filled up with, which is every chain recipe followed by every filler recipe.

    • CHAINS_NESTED

      public static final List<CommandGenerateCrafting.CraftingGenerationHelper.CraftingChain> CHAINS_NESTED
      The subset of CHAINS that requires at least 4 planks per craft. A planks recipe yields 4 planks at a time, so a request for at least 4 planks can never be fully satisfied by the leftovers of a previous craft, which means such a chain keeps requiring a nested planks job for as long as the benchmark runs.

    • placeWriterCell

      public static org.cyclops.integrateddynamics.api.part.PartPos placeWriterCell(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos cell, net.minecraft.world.item.Item item, boolean ignoreStorage)
      Turn the given cell into a crafting writer that continuously requests the given item. The cell itself is left empty: the crafting writer aspect only operates on the network, so it does not need a target block.

      level - The level.
      cell - The cell position.
      item - The item to request.
      ignoreStorage - If the writer should request the item even when it is already in storage. This is what turns a single craft into a continuous stream of crafting jobs.
      Returns:
      The position of the crafting writer.

    • generateInterfacesIdle

      public static void generateInterfacesIdle(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos startPos, int size)
      Generate a grid where every cell holds a crafting table with an idle crafting interface in front of it, each holding a single recipe. Nothing ever requests a craft here, so this isolates the standing cost of crafting interfaces: their part ticks, their recipe registrations, and their presence in the crafting network.

    • generateInterfacesIdleRecipes

      public static void generateInterfacesIdleRecipes(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos startPos, int size)
      As generateInterfacesIdle(ServerLevel, BlockPos, int), but with every crafting interface completely filled with recipes. Compared to generateInterfacesIdle(ServerLevel, BlockPos, int), this scales up the network's recipe index without changing the number of parts.

    • generateCraftSimple

      public static void generateCraftSimple(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos startPos, int size)
      Generate a grid where crafting writers continuously request items that are crafted out of planks that are already present in network storage. This isolates the cost of scheduling and executing a stream of single-step crafting jobs.

    • generateCraftNested

      public static void generateCraftNested(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos startPos, int size)
      Generate a grid where crafting writers continuously request items whose ingredients are themselves not in storage, and must first be crafted out of logs. Compared to generateCraftSimple(ServerLevel, BlockPos, int), every request additionally has to resolve and schedule a dependency graph of crafting jobs.

    • generateCraftRecipeIndex

      public static void generateCraftRecipeIndex(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos startPos, int size)
      As generateCraftSimple(ServerLevel, BlockPos, int), but with every crafting interface completely filled with recipes. This scales up the network's recipe index, which every crafting job calculation has to search.

    • generateCraftSatisfiedIdle

      public static void generateCraftSatisfiedIdle(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos startPos, int size)
      As generateCraftSimple(ServerLevel, BlockPos, int), but with writers that request an item that is already in storage. No crafting job is ever scheduled, so this isolates the cost that a crafting writer pays per tick just to determine that there is nothing to do.

    • getPartProblems

      public static List<String> getPartProblems(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerLevel level, net.minecraft.core.BlockPos startPos, int size)
      Collect everything that is wrong with the parts of a generated grid. A part that failed to activate, or whose active aspect is in an error state, silently does nothing while still costing tick time, which would turn a benchmark preset into an expensive no-op.
      Parameters:
      level - The level.
      startPos - The lowest corner of the grid.
      size - The edge length of the grid.
      Returns:
      A description of every broken part, empty if all parts are healthy.
